title: Attorney General of Connecticut

context.text: Connecticut's Secretary of the State publishes November 3, 2026 sample ballots; the Hamden sample ballot and CT Mirror's October 19 voter guide show William Tong (Democratic, also on the Working Families Party line) and John Bolton (Republican) for Attorney General.
Both major-party primaries for this office were canceled because each candidate was unopposed.

candidates.name: William Tong
candidates.ballotNote: Cross-endorsed by the Working Families Party; seeking a third term.

summary.text: William Tong is the incumbent Democratic Attorney General, elected in 2018 after six terms as a state representative. CT Mirror reports he has filed or joined more than 40 lawsuits challenging federal policies since Donald Trump returned to office.

background.text: Litigator and former state representative (six terms); the first Asian American elected to state office in Connecticut.
Elected Attorney General in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.

priorities.text: Challenging federal policies in court, including the president's efforts to end birthright citizenship, per CT Mirror.

record.text: Joined a coalition of 26 states, counties and cities on October 2, 2026 in suing the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration over its final rule weakening fuel-economy standards, in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit.
Joined a coalition of 25 states, counties and cities on October 1, 2026 petitioning the D.C. Circuit to strike down the EPA's repeal of greenhouse-gas limits for power plants.
Announced a $625,000 settlement on October 16, 2026 with Frontier Communications over an April 2024 data breach affecting 58,841 Connecticut residents.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website was reached; positions on the guide's fixed issues were not found as his own direct statements.

candidates.name: John Bolton
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated unopposed; the Republican primary was canceled.

summary.text: John Bolton is the Republican nominee, a Westport lawyer with a mostly solo practice who has served on the town Planning and Zoning Commission. He ran unsuccessfully for state representative in 2024 and says the Attorney General's office has spent too much time on lawsuits against the Trump administration.

background.text: Attorney for 35 years, mostly as an independent lawyer, with stints as in-house counsel for companies in upstate New York and Alabama; a native of West Hartford who has lived in Westport since 1997.

Served on the Westport Planning and Zoning Commission from 2021 (full commissioner since 2023), according to the Westport Journal in March 2026; CT Mirror's October 19 voter guide describes him as having formerly served.
Holds a law degree from the University of Connecticut and a bachelor's degree from Clark University.

priorities.text: Prioritizing the rule of law over what he called "political advocacy" by the Attorney General's office.
Election integrity, which he says needs to be addressed to restore confidence.

Enforcing consumer-protection laws, supporting law enforcement and victims, challenging policies that raise energy prices, defending parental rights, and holding those who misuse taxpayer dollars accountable, per his BallotReady profile.

statements.quote: I'm not sure that a state should be opining about tariffs
statements.context: In a March 2026 interview with the Westport Journal on the role of the Attorney General

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign website could not be reached. No record of elected office.
